stories.title: Israel’s election count leaves Netanyahu and Eisenkot both short of a majority
stories.summary: With about 84% of ballots counted, the Times of Israel reports Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc on 54 seats, Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc on 49 and Arab parties on 17, with 61 needed for a majority in the 120-seat [[knesset|Knesset]]. The BBC says neither main bloc looks able to govern without relying on Arab parties, and both leaders have said they will form the next government. Al Jazeera reports that Tel Aviv’s benchmark share index fell more than 3 percent on the uncertainty.
stories.background: This was Israel’s first general election since the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023 and the wars that followed, and it was widely described as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership. Israel has only ever been governed by coalitions.

stories.title: At least 30 people die as two high-speed trains collide in central Spain
stories.summary: The Guardian and DW report that at least 30 people were killed on Wednesday when one high-speed train ran into the back of another in Toledo province, knocking two carriages off the track. Early reports gave a lower toll of at least 10, and officials warn it may rise. The Japan Times quotes a regional spokesperson saying 147 people were on one train and 397 on the other; rail service between Madrid and Andalusia has been suspended.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, and Africa’s health agency warns it could spread further
stories.summary: DR Congo has reported more than 10,000 Ebola cases and nearly 4,900 deaths, DW reports via AllAfrica, in an outbreak with no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The Guardian says Jean Kaseya of the Africa CDC warns the “unprecedented” spread could reach the UK unless more funding is found for preparedness. BBC News reported on Tuesday that Kenya has confirmed nine cases.

stories.title: Defeated Brazilian candidate Flávio Bolsonaro leaves the country as Washington offers visas
stories.summary: Argentina’s government says Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday’s presidential runoff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, crossed into Argentina and is on his way to Ecuador, the BBC and RTÉ report. NPR says the US will issue visas to him and his family, and that he left after a money-laundering probe and a missed court deadline to surrender his passports. His party has accepted Lula’s win, but he has not conceded, and President Trump has called the vote “rigged” without offering evidence.

stories.title: Qatar puts a new draft deal to Iran as the US war bill passes $47 billion
stories.summary: An official briefed on the talks says Qatari mediators gave Iran a new draft deal to end the war with the US and Israel on Sunday, and that Tehran is expected to reply by the end of the week. Reuters reports, via Daily Maverick, Pentagon data showing the US has spent more than $47 billion on the war, over 25% above July’s estimate. The Times of Israel reports, citing a report, that Washington has warned Gulf states of a possible renewed offensive after the US midterms.
stories.background: The US and Israel began the war with Iran earlier this year, and it has disrupted shipping and fuel supplies through the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]] and across the region.

stories.title: A local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky holds for 30 hours and is extended across Kherson region
stories.summary: France 24 reports the truce in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky held through its first day and night, even as fighting continued elsewhere. The BBC says the ceasefire has been extended across Ukraine’s Kherson region, and that Russia and Ukraine report no breaches. Elsewhere, the Kyiv Independent says Russian strikes killed two people and injured 17 in the past day.
stories.background: The BBC says the truce was brokered by Melania Trump and was first planned for stranded residents of Oleshky, a city that has had no electricity, gas or water for three years.

The Financial Times, cited by the Kyiv Independent, says Putin lectured the two leaders on medieval history and said little about an immediate ceasefire. President Zelensky backed the call, praising the leaders for being open about it.

He called it a terrorist act and raised the terror alert to its highest level, Balkan Insight says.
